lines.speaker: COURT GUARD
lines.text: Back. All four of you, back against the wall.
lines.sfx_cue: court corridor, handcuffs and crowd murmurs

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: Let me speak to the judge. Two minutes. That woman is alive.

lines.speaker: COURT GUARD
lines.text: You will speak when your case number is called.

lines.speaker: naresh
lines.text: Our case number belongs to a dead woman. Bring her inside.

lines.speaker: WOMAN IN CROWD
lines.text: Eighteen months in jail, and now the murdered woman walks into court.

lines.speaker: COURT GUARD
lines.text: Quiet. This is a court corridor, not the village square.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: They were jailed in my name. I want to hear why.

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: Meera... you are really standing here.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Yes. Now tell me how my life became your murder charge.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Salim, stop. You don't know who is listening.

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: Everyone listened when they called us murderers.

lines.speaker: pintu
lines.text: And everyone watched when police dragged us from our houses.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: You will each get an opportunity. Do not coordinate your accounts here.

lines.speaker: naresh
lines.text: Coordinate? We have shared one cell and one accusation for eighteen months.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Then eighteen months should have taught you to answer separately.

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: My answer was separate. I gave it on the first night.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: What answer?

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: That Raghav sent us to the accident site.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Salim!

lines.speaker: COURT GUARD
lines.text: No shouting between prisoners.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Say it again. Clearly.

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: Raghav told us where to go, before the police arrived there.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Do not add another word in this corridor.

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: Madam, I already said every word. Police wrote it down.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: Case number forty-seven. State versus Salim, Naresh, Pintu and Irfan.

lines.speaker: COURT GUARD
lines.text: Move.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Four men entered together. For the first time, the woman they were accused of murdering entered behind them.
lines.sfx_cue: chains and footsteps enter high-ceilinged courtroom

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: Who authorised this crowd? Clear the centre aisle.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: The villagers are witnesses to the identity dispute, Your Honour.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: They are spectators until summoned. Spectators remain silent.

lines.speaker: WOMAN IN GALLERY
lines.text: They called Salim a butcher in front of his mother.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: One more interruption, and the gallery will be emptied.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: The police request permission to place a new development on record.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: Proceed.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Meera's death certificate was formally marked disputed yesterday.

lines.speaker: naresh
lines.text: Then open these cuffs.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: You will not instruct the court.

lines.speaker: naresh
lines.text: No, sir. I... I only mean, there cannot be her murder if she is here.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: A disputed certificate is not an acquittal. It is a reason to examine the record.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Examine the part where they used my name without asking whether I was alive.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: You will be heard after the case history is read.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: The prosecution alleged that the four accused killed Meera and burned her body near the east quarry road.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: They were detained after being located near the accident site.

lines.speaker: pintu
lines.text: Because somebody called us there.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: Who called you?

lines.speaker: pintu
lines.text: Salim said there was a crashed vehicle. He said people might need help.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: Salim, where did you get that information?

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Sir, may I speak privately before he answers?

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: No. The question was not addressed to you.

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: Raghav came to the repair shed that morning.

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: He said a vehicle had gone off the east quarry road.

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: He told us to reach it before the traffic police took everything away.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: What time?

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: A little after six. The tea stall had just opened.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: Was Raghav with you at the site?

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: No. He gave the location, then left in his white pickup.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Why did all four of you go?

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: Pintu knew the road. Naresh had a tow chain. Irfan came because I asked.

lines.speaker: naresh
lines.text: We found a burned vehicle, one body, and no living passenger.

lines.speaker: pintu
lines.text: Police arrived within twelve minutes. Too quickly for that road.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: How were the accused connected to the alleged victim?

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: The original case diary says they were found beside the body and gave inconsistent accounts.

lines.speaker: naresh
lines.text: We were questioned separately after being awake all night.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: They kept asking which one of us lit the fire.

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: I kept saying Raghav sent us.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Did you sign that statement?

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: Every page. My thumbprint is below the last line.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: Sub-inspector, locate the first-night statement.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Court clerk, give me volume one.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: Arrest memos, seizure list, site sketch and medical forms.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Where are the individual statements?

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: After page eighty-six, according to the index.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Page eighty-six is followed by page ninety-three.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: Check the supplementary volume.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: Supplementary volume begins with laboratory correspondence.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Ask who removed seven pages.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: The court will ask the questions.

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: My statement was five pages. The others signed one page each.

lines.speaker: pintu
lines.text: Seven pages.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: Don't... don't say anything else, Salim.

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: You stayed quiet for your brother. I stayed quiet because I trusted the file.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Clerk, read the index entry aloud.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: Accused statements, pages eighty-seven through ninety-three, recorded on the night of arrest.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: And those pages are not in either volume?

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: No, Your Honour.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: The original case diary contains the index, but Salim's statement is missing.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: These men will not be returned to silence inside the old murder file.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: Your Honour, the prison transfer order is ready.

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: Read it aloud. Their families have waited long enough to hear it.

lines.speaker: COURT CLERK
lines.text: All four accused are to be produced in the reopened identity inquiry.

lines.speaker: naresh
lines.text: Does that mean we leave jail today?

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: It means the old accusation may no longer bury new evidence.

lines.speaker: salim
lines.text: And my missing statement?

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: The police will reconstruct its custody and record your account again.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: In open court?

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: Under protection, if the investigating officer finds a credible risk.

lines.speaker: irfan
lines.text: I need protection for my brother, not for myself.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Give me his details before you return to custody.

lines.speaker: pintu
lines.text: We came to court as four murderers.

lines.speaker: naresh
lines.text: We are still in cuffs.

lines.speaker: pintu
lines.text: Yes. But now the court has to ask who sent us there.

lines.speaker: WOMAN IN GALLERY
lines.text: Naresh, your daughter can hear you!
lines.sfx_cue: gallery erupts in cries and applause

lines.speaker: JUDGE
lines.text: Order. The four accused will be brought into the reopened inquiry, not hidden inside the old case.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Before noon, an old missing-person complaint reached the court records tray. No named witness saw who placed it there.
lines.sfx_cue: single paper slides into metal tray

lines.speaker: COURT GUARD
lines.text: Clear the doorway. The next matter cannot enter through your shoulders.
lines.sfx_cue: court veranda crowd and approaching bus horn

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: Please, move. I came from the neighbouring district for the burned woman.
lines.sfx_cue: hurried footsteps, cloth bag buckle rattles

lines.speaker: COURT GUARD
lines.text: Which burned woman?

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: The woman cremated as Meera. She may be my sister.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: What is your sister's name?

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: Kesar.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Come inside. Do not tell this story in a doorway.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: You are Meera?

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: Then whose ashes did they give your family?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Nobody has established that those ashes belonged to her sister.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: Are you the man who identified the body?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: I am her father.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: That was not my question.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Janki, come to the side room. Bring every document you have.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: I brought her missing-person complaint and three photographs.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: When did Kesar disappear?

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: In June, twenty twenty-one. She left for a hospital appointment and never returned.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: What made you connect her to this body?

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: A court notice said the woman wore a black thread around her wrist.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Many women wear black thread.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: Kesar's had three knots and a small copper bead.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: The original hospital note mentions a black thread. It does not mention a bead.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: Then look at the photograph before they cut it away.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: The photograph is disturbing. Confirm that you still want to view it.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: I have imagined worse every night for seventeen months. Show me.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: You don't have to prove your love by looking at a burned face.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: No. I have to prove the police searched under the wrong woman's name.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Only the wrist photograph first.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: The thread is twisted twice here. Kesar always did that after bathing.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: That cannot identify a person.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: Neither could you, apparently.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: You arrived ten minutes ago. Do not judge what that day was.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: My sister vanished. Your daughter returned. I know exactly what these days are.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Enough. We test records, not grief against grief.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Did Kesar have a tattoo?

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: No permanent tattoo. A childhood burn mark below her left thumb.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: The body photograph showed a tattoo on the hand opposite mine.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: The skin was damaged. The mark was difficult to read.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: Was her face visible?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: This interview is being conducted by the police.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: You answer very carefully for a grieving father.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Janki, what hospital appointment was Kesar attending?

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: A wrist dressing. The burn had reopened after field work.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Which hospital?

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: The district civil hospital. I wrote it in the complaint.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Babulal, bring the unidentified-body intake sheet from the original file.

lines.speaker: babulal
lines.text: The original is brittle. I will place it in a clear sleeve.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: Why is there a red line across the name box?

lines.speaker: babulal
lines.text: The patient arrived unidentified. Meera's name was added after Devraj's identification.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: After police asked me to identify my daughter.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: You identified a thread and a damaged mark. Not me.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: I identified what I could.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: The intake sheet records one female patient, severe burns, no usable facial identification.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: Read the number at the top.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: D H P, twenty-one, zero six one four, thirty-eight.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: No... read it once more.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: D H P, twenty-one, zero six one four, thirty-eight.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: That number was written by the hospital clerk on Kesar's appointment slip.

lines.speaker: babulal
lines.text: Your missing-person complaint is in the records tray. It has the same number in the reference box.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Show her the complaint.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: D H P, twenty-one, zero six one four, thirty-eight. This hospital intake number is the number on Kesar's missing-person complaint.

lines.speaker: MAN IN CROWD
lines.text: Devraj, look at your daughter before you deny her again.
lines.sfx_cue: village courtyard crowd and microphone feedback

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: I will not answer a mob.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Then answer me. Touch my hand and say who I am.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: This public spectacle proves nothing.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: It proved enough when you called Ma a stranger in front of everyone.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: Mohan, stand beside me.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Nobody will touch or surround Devraj. He is here to correct his identification statement.

lines.speaker: WOMAN IN CROWD
lines.text: He sent four men to jail with that statement.

lines.speaker: MAN IN CROWD
lines.text: And he would not even touch Meera at the station.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Silence. Public humiliation will not repair public error.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: No. But public truth may begin to repair it.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: You asked me to attend a formal verification. Conduct it formally.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: I intend to. Stand at the microphone.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: I can speak from here.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Your original identification was accepted publicly. Your correction will be heard publicly.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: You have already marked the certificate disputed.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: A red seal corrected a document. It did not correct your words.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Devraj crossed the same courtyard where his refusal had made Meera a stranger.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: The microphone is unnecessary.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: The people at the back disagree.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: So does the family of the woman you identified.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: The body has not been proved to be Kesar.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: No. But the hospital number proved my complaint was ignored.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Today's question is narrower. What did Devraj actually see?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: I saw the body police brought from the accident site.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Could you identify the face?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: The face was... it was severely burned.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: That was not the question.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: No. I could not identify the face.

lines.speaker: WOMAN IN CROWD
lines.text: He never saw her face, yet he called it Meera!

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: One more interruption, and I will end the verification.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Do not end it. I waited eighteen months for this answer.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Devraj, what feature did you rely upon first?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: A dark mark on the hand.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: You described it as Meera's tattoo.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: That is what I believed it was.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Meera's tattoo is on the opposite hand.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: I know that now.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: You knew which hand when I was a child. You paid for the medicine after it became infected.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: The body was covered. The room smelled of smoke and chemicals.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: What other feature did you rely upon?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: The black thread around the wrist.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: Kesar wore one with three knots and a copper bead.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: I did not see a bead.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Did Meera always wear a black thread?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: She wore one during illness and after temple visits.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Not every day. I had removed mine before I disappeared.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: It was tied to the bedpost. I found it after she was gone.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: You never told me that.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: You never asked me. You told me Ma was dead.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: Then you burned someone and said she was Ma.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Mohan, you are too young to understand that day.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: I understood the day you would not touch her.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Devraj, did any doctor certify a facial identification before you signed?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Did police have fingerprints or DNA linking the body to Meera?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Not then.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Did you see clothing you personally recognised?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Only burned cloth. Nothing certain.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Then state why you signed the identification.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Police said the accident matched the time she vanished.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: They said the four men near the site had changed their stories.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: They showed me the hand, the thread, and her name already written on a form.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: My name was already written?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: In pencil, at the top. I thought they knew more than they told me.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: That detail is not in your original statement.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Nobody asked who wrote the name first.

lines.speaker: janki
lines.text: They gave you a name, and you gave them certainty.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: They asked whether it could be my daughter.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: And you turned could be into yes.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: I was afraid.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Of what?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Of taking an unclaimed body home. Of refusing, then learning I had abandoned you twice.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: So you accepted the first answer that ended the waiting.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: State it without explanation. Did you identify the face?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: kavita
lines.text: Was your identification based on certainty?

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: No. It was based on fear and grief.

lines.speaker: WOMAN IN CROWD
lines.text: Then Meera was shamed because her father was frightened.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Yes. She was shamed because I was frightened.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: At the station, I asked you to touch my hand.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: I remember.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: You called me an impostor where my children could hear later.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: I was trying to protect the decision I had already made.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Not me. The decision.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: mohan
lines.text: Touch her hand now.

lines.speaker: tara
lines.text: No. Let Ma choose whether he may.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: You may touch my hand after you answer one question.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Ask it.

lines.speaker: meera
lines.text: Who am I? Say it so the whole village hears you.

lines.speaker: devraj
lines.text: Meera is my daughter. I was wrong to call her a stranger.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Salim told Meera and Kavita that Raghav had directed the four accused to the accident site before police arrived.

state_changes.fact: He publicly implicated Raghav in directing the accused to the accident site.
A jailed accused publicly connected him to the accident site before police arrival.

beat_sheet.what_happened: The court heard that the four men were charged after police found them beside the burned body and treated their accounts as inconsistent.

state_changes.fact: The public basis for his murder charge was stated in court.
The public basis for his murder charge was stated in court.
The public basis for his murder charge was stated in court.
The public basis for his murder charge was stated in court.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Salim stated under court questioning that Raghav gave him the east quarry road location shortly after six in the morning.

state_changes.fact: His account of receiving the accident location from Raghav entered the reopened hearing.
He was accused in court of knowing the accident location before police arrived.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Kavita and the court clerk established that the indexed pages containing Salim's first-night statement were missing from the original case diary.

state_changes.fact: Pages eighty-seven through ninety-three, including Salim's statement, were missing.
His claim that his statement had been omitted gained documentary support from the page gap.

beat_sheet.what_happened: A copy of Kesar's missing-person complaint was placed in the court records tray before Janki's interview.

state_changes.fact: The complaint became available in the court records tray without an identified source.

beat_sheet.note: No named character was present when the complaint was placed in the tray, leaving its delivery as deliberate open canon.

beat_sheet.what_happened: The court ordered all four accused produced in the reopened identity inquiry and directed police to record Salim's account again.

state_changes.fact: He was moved from being contained solely in the old murder case into the reopened inquiry.
He was moved from being contained solely in the old murder case into the reopened inquiry.
He was moved from being contained solely in the old murder case into the reopened inquiry.
He was moved from being contained solely in the old murder case into the reopened inquiry.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Janki stated that the burned body might be her missing sister Kesar and described Kesar's black wrist thread, copper bead and left-hand burn mark.

state_changes.fact: She formally connected Kesar's disappearance to the unidentified burned body.
Kesar became a documented possible identity for the body cremated as Meera.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Janki recognised the burned body's hospital intake number as the same number recorded on Kesar's missing-person complaint.

state_changes.fact: She found a direct record-number link between Kesar's complaint and the burned body.
The hospital intake record became linked to Kesar's missing-person file.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Kavita required Devraj to correct his original identification publicly before the same village that had witnessed his rejection of Meera.

state_changes.fact: He was required to answer publicly for the identification he had previously defended.
She gained a public forum to challenge her father's rejection.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Devraj admitted that he could not see the burned body's face and relied on a hand mark, black thread and Meera's name already written on a form.

state_changes.fact: He withdrew any claim that he had visually identified the body's face.
Its factual basis was publicly reduced to ambiguous physical details and a prewritten name.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Devraj stated that fear and grief, rather than certainty, caused him to sign the body identification.

state_changes.fact: He publicly accepted responsibility for converting uncertainty into a positive identification.
Her father's stated basis for declaring her dead was publicly discredited.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Devraj publicly called Meera his daughter and admitted that he had been wrong to call her a stranger.

state_changes.fact: Her father publicly recognised her as his daughter.
He publicly reversed his rejection of Meera.
She witnessed Devraj recognise Meera as his daughter.
He witnessed Devraj recognise Meera as his daughter.

promise_ledger.how_paid: The court stated that the four men were charged after being found beside the burned body, and Salim revealed that Raghav had directed them to the accident site before police arrived.

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: Whose body was cremated after being wrongly identified as Meera?
How did Raghav know the exact five-lakh-rupee payment date before Meera disclosed the amount?

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: Does the matching hospital number prove that the burned woman was Kesar?
Who wrote Meera's name on the unidentified-body form before Devraj signed the identification?

dates_fixed.what: Meera enters Dharmapur police station and discovers that she remains recorded as dead.
Kavita conducts the initial private identity test and finds the tattoo-hand discrepancy.
Meera visits her former house under police guard and the bus stand photograph arrives.
Raghav gives his account before the village committee and reveals knowledge of a payment dated 2021-05-03.
Meera identifies room twelve in Kota, Mohan publicly calls her Ma and the rental ledger reveals a disputed signature dated 2021-06-21.
Kavita conducts the open identity verification and Meera's death certificate is marked disputed.
The four jailed accused appear in court, Salim implicates Raghav and his indexed statement is found missing from the case diary.
The court brings the four accused into the reopened inquiry, and Janki links Kesar's complaint to the burned body's hospital intake number.
Devraj admits that fear and grief caused the mistaken identification and publicly recognises Meera as his daughter.

periods_fixed.elapsed: No time elapsed; both episodes occur on 2022-11-14.
